title: Rina and Lina are the SAME name in Korean 😅 #learnkorean
caption:
In Hangul, R and L are one letter: ㄹ.
So Rina and Lina are both 리나 (ri-na) — and Ryan and Lion are both 라이언 (ra-i-eon) 🦁

More names:
Laura → 로라 (ro-ra)
Ryan → 라이언 (ra-i-eon)

ㄹ sounds like a light tap, somewhere between r and l. Korean doesn't tell R and L apart, so one cup can have two owners ☕

Got an R or L in your name? Comment it — I'll write it in Hangul ✍️
Try your own name: synk.im/name/

alt: A needle-felted neighborhood cafe. The barista doll holds up one cup whose sleeve says 리나 and calls 리나! Two felt customers, Rina and Lina, both stand up and shout 저요! (Me!). They grab the same cup from both sides and pull, while the coral felt mascot Mongle is squeezed between them: 내 커피… (my coffee…). In Korean, R and L are one letter, ㄹ, so Rina and Lina are both 리나. The barista brings two 리나 cups and both are happy, but Mongle still has no cup: 내 커피는…? Then the barista calls 라이언! Ryan stands up — and so does a felt lion, roaring 어흥! 저요! because Lion is also 라이언. Ryan and the lion pull the same cup, until the lion swallows it whole (꿀꺽!) and Ryan is left holding only the empty sleeve. R or L in your name? Comment it.
